title: Setting Up a Data Engineering Dev Environment

scenes.title: Setting Up a Data Engineering Dev Environment
scenes.narration: A well-configured development environment is the foundation that makes every later data engineering task smoother and more reliable.

scenes.title: The Essential Toolkit
bullets: A version manager pins your Python version so projects stay consistent.
Virtual environments isolate each project's dependencies from the rest.
Git and an SSH key connect you to shared repositories and servers.
A capable editor with linting keeps your code clean as you write it.
scenes.narration: A strong setup rests on a few pillars. A version manager like pyenv locks each project to a specific Python so behavior never drifts. Virtual environments then isolate the libraries per project. Git plus a configured SSH key give you access to repositories and remote machines, and a good editor with linting catches mistakes the moment you make them.

scenes.title: Bootstrapping a Project
scenes.narration: Onboarding to a project follows a predictable path. You clone the repository, create and activate a virtual environment, then install the pinned requirements. After copying secrets into a local .env file, you run the test suite to confirm everything works before writing a line of your own.

scenes.title: A Repeatable Setup
scenes.code:
git clone git@github.com:team/pipeline.git
cd pipeline
python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env   # then fill in secrets
pytest
scenes.narration: This script captures a clean onboarding in six lines. It clones over SSH, moves into the project, and spins up an isolated environment in one combined command. Installing from requirements guarantees the same versions as the team, copying the example env file gives you a template for secrets, and pytest verifies the setup end to end.

scenes.text: Document your setup so a new teammate can be productive in minutes — reproducibility is a feature, not an afterthought.
scenes.narration: Treat a fast, documented setup as part of the product. When anyone can bootstrap the project in minutes, the whole team moves faster and more confidently.
